SPANISH: Hace cientos de años que en hermoso día apareció en el valle de Mexico un hombre blanco con cabello y barba negra...
LITERAL ENGLISH: Hundreds of years ago, on a beautiful day, a white man with black hair and beard appeared in the Valley of Mexico...
FAITHFUL ENGLISH: Long ago, on a radiant day, a white man with dark hair and beard appeared in the Valley of Mexico...
CULTURAL CONTEXT: The man described likely reflects mythic interpretations of Quetzalcoatl, blending indigenous and later Spanish descriptions.
TRANSLATION CLARIFICATION: Faithful version softens and naturalizes 'hombre blanco' as mythic figure rather than literal man.

SPANISH: Pronto se reunió a él un gran número de gente que crecía según el día avanzaba. Era Quetzalcoatl...
LITERAL ENGLISH: Soon many people gathered around him as the day went on. He was Quetzalcoatl...
FAITHFUL ENGLISH: Soon crowds gathered, drawn to him as the day passed. This was Quetzalcoatl...
CULTURAL CONTEXT: Quetzalcoatl became revered as 'Dios Blanco', associated with moral teachings and peaceful leadership.
TRANSLATION CLARIFICATION: Faithful version adds 'drawn to him' to clarify imagery of gathering.

SPANISH: Durante su permanencia allí hizo construir casas de oración y penitencia que consistían de grandes salones...
LITERAL ENGLISH: During his stay he built houses of prayer and penitence consisting of large halls...
FAITHFUL ENGLISH: While there, he built great prayer halls and places for penitence...
CULTURAL CONTEXT: Quetzalcoatl promoted a moral code focused on prayer, confession, and rejection of human sacrifice.
TRANSLATION CLARIFICATION: Faithful version smooths 'houses of prayer and penitence' into natural phrasing.

SPANISH: Fue un rey sacerdote muy sabio; enseñó a muchos otros reyes a gobernar...
LITERAL ENGLISH: He was a very wise king-priest; he taught many other kings to rule...
FAITHFUL ENGLISH: He was a wise priest-king, instructing many rulers in wisdom and discretion...
CULTURAL CONTEXT: Depicts Quetzalcoatl's role as a moral and political teacher across generations.
TRANSLATION CLARIFICATION: Faithful version rearranges 'king-priest' into natural English order 'priest-king'.

SPANISH: Pronto se confundió con el planeta Venus y se convirtió en el dios del viento.
LITERAL ENGLISH: Soon he was confused with the planet Venus and became the god of the wind.
FAITHFUL ENGLISH: In time, he merged with the planet Venus and became the god of the wind.
CULTURAL CONTEXT: Quetzalcoatl was mythologically linked to Venus as both a morning star and divine presence.
TRANSLATION CLARIFICATION: 'Merged with' better conveys mythic transformation than 'confused with'.
